messages:
Jada Williams: Looking for an arch/security review on the A/B exposure logging design before we lock ADR. This is for route-level A/B testing (Console-first) and we’ll be using exposure logs as the source of truth for experiment denominators + per-variant aggregations.

Jada Williams: Doc draft (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/ab-exposure-logging-draft
Key topics we need eyes on: privacy/PII constraints, retention, and metric/event cardinality guardrails. @Marcus Lin @Naomi Feldman @Kevin Osei @Allison Grant @Logan Wright would love feedback.

Ravi Menon: +1. Also want to make sure this doesn’t fight with routing fallbacks. We’re emitting exposure at gateway after assignment, before upstream request fanout.

Logan Wright: Skimmed the doc. Main questions:
1) Are we storing “events” (row per request) or counters (metrics)?
2) What dimensions are mandatory? We need to avoid a 10x explosion if someone tags user-supplied headers.

Allison Grant: From obs side: please do NOT put raw route paths in the tag set. We’ve been burned by /v1/foo/{id} and query strings. We need either a normalized route ID (config ID) or something like “route_template”.

Jordan Lee: On assignment side we currently compute bucket based on a hash input. The doc suggests using `tenant_id + api_key_id + stable_user_key` (header). That header is the scary part.

Marcus Lin: Security hat: “stable_user_key” is fine only if (a) it’s customer-provided and (b) we NEVER store it in plaintext. Prefer: we store *only* a salted hash, and the salt is internal (not shared), rotated w/ documented blast radius.

Naomi Feldman: Agree w/ Marcus. Also we need clarity on whether exposure logs are considered “customer content” (like prompts) vs platform telemetry. Either way, we should enforce: no prompt, no completion text, no full request bodies.

Nadia Rahman: Cost attribution needs experiment_id + variant_id to join token/GPU meters. But we don’t need request_id for cost; we only need per-request token counts aggregated by variant. Request_id would make it easier to debug though.

Mina Haddad: Where exactly do you emit? If we emit at gateway, but request fails pre-upstream (auth, rate limit), is that still “exposure”? For analysis, I’d want to distinguish “assigned” vs “served”.

Jada Williams: Good call. Current proposal:
- exposure event emitted when assignment decision is made AND request is eligible for the experiment.
- separate “served_variant” metric emitted when upstream request actually executes on that variant.
- include outcome tags like `decision=assigned|bypassed` and `served=true|false`? (open question)

Logan Wright: Careful: outcome tags add cardinality but if it’s low-cardinality enums it’s fine. I’d rather have explicit fields than infer from missing values.

Allison Grant: +1 low-card enums are ok. Please don’t add `error_message` / `stack` as tags. If you need debugging, use logs/traces separately.

Ravi Menon: Another edge: retries + streaming reconnect. We want stable assignment; the gateway may see multiple connections for the same logical request. How do we avoid counting multiple exposures?

Jordan Lee: We can use a sticky assignment key that survives retries, but only if client sends idempotency key. Otherwise we can’t dedupe perfectly.

Jada Williams: For v1 we were leaning:
- If `Idempotency-Key` present, include a hashed form to dedupe in analytics (NOT stored raw).
- If not present, accept some double-counting; it should be small and symmetric across variants.

Marcus Lin: Please don’t create a quasi-user-tracking system via idempotency keys. If you hash them, fine. But keep retention short for raw events.

Kevin Osei: On retention + audit: For telemetry in our lake, typical is 30 days raw, 13 months aggregated. For *experiment reporting* customers might expect longer. But I think we can support “reporting window” from aggregates, not raw.

Naomi Feldman: Also access controls: who can query raw exposure events? Ideally only SRE/Telemetry on-call + a small allowlist. Console should read pre-aggregated tables keyed by org/project/experiment.

Logan Wright: +1. If we allow ad-hoc raw queries we will inevitably leak something via joined datasets.

Allison Grant: What are the planned dimensions? Need an explicit allowlist.

Jada Williams: Proposed exposure schema (high level):
- required: `ts`, `org_id`, `project_id`, `environment`, `experiment_id`, `variant_id`, `route_id`, `region`, `deployment_mode` (hosted/dedicated), `result` (assigned/bypassed), `schema_version`
- optional: `model_id` (normalized), `http_status_class` (2xx/4xx/5xx), `error_type` (timeout/429/upstream)
- optional hashed: `sticky_key_hash` (derived), `idempotency_key_hash` (if present)
No prompts, no headers, no full URL.

Mina Haddad: `route_id` should be the config object id (control-plane). Not “/v1/chat/completions”. A single customer can have multiple routes with same path but diff policies.

Ravi Menon: Agree. Also include `policy_revision`? so we know which version of the config was live.

Allison Grant: Policy revision is fine if it’s small cardinality. It might churn if customers are editing frequently though.

Logan Wright: Better: include `experiment_revision` as an integer that increments on update. We can store that in control plane and stamp it into the event.

Nadia Rahman: For cost, we also need to know which “variant config” (model + parameters) is in play. But please don’t add temperature/top_p/etc as dimensions.

Jada Williams: Yep, no param dims. We’ll capture the variant config in control plane metadata and surface it in Console via config fetch, not via telemetry tags.

Marcus Lin: Privacy note: `org_id`/`project_id` are internal identifiers and ok. The only sensitive bits are anything derived from user identity or request content. Hashing sticky keys should be salted and non-reversible. Also document that customers must not put emails/usernames in the stable header.

Naomi Feldman: We should add Console copy + docs: “Use opaque IDs only (UUIDs). Do not send PII.” And enforce length/charset to reduce accidental PII.

Jordan Lee: On deterministic assignment input, we can allow:
- org_id (always)
- project_id (optional)
- api_key_id (optional)
- `x-redwood-sticky-key` (optional, customer provided)
Then compute `sticky_key_hash = HMAC_SHA256(internal_salt, concat(fields))`
We never persist the preimage.

Allison Grant: Cardinality limits: we should hard cap number of active experiments per org? Or at least enforce per-metric series limits.

Logan Wright: We can enforce on ingestion:
- allowlist tag keys
- max tag value length (e.g., 64)
- drop/normalize unknown `model_id`
- reject if experiment_id/variant_id not registered (prevents random IDs)

Kevin Osei: Retention proposal:
- raw exposure events: 30 days
- aggregated experiment rollups (hourly): 400 days (13 months)
- audit logs for config changes: per audit policy (currently 2 years for enterprise)
This matches most compliance asks.

Mina Haddad: I like separating audit vs telemetry. Exposure logs shouldn’t be used to reconstruct “who saw what” beyond aggregate.

Jada Williams: +1. We’re explicitly NOT trying to do per-user experiment analysis.

Ravi Menon: One more: sampling. Are we sampling exposures? If we sample, denominators get messy.

Logan Wright: Don’t sample denominators. If we need to reduce cost, use counters/metrics for exposures and sample only detailed traces. But if you’re doing event rows, we should aim for 100% with minimal fields.

Allison Grant: If 100% events, we need to be sure the pipeline can handle QPS. Otherwise we’ll drop and bias results. Metrics counters might be safer.

Nadia Rahman: Counters also integrate better with our existing per-route token/cost meters. But Console wants drilldowns. Are drilldowns required for v1?

Jada Williams: v1 requirement is mostly experiment-level and variant-level graphs (latency/cost/errors + exposures). No per-request drilldown in Console.
So I’m ok shifting to “metrics-first” for exposures (counters), with optional sampled event logs for debugging gated to internal.

Marcus Lin: Strong preference for metrics-first. Raw events are a bigger privacy surface.

Naomi Feldman: Agree. If we keep any raw events, make them internal-only with a separate dataset + short retention (7–14 days).

Jada Williams: OK, proposal update from this thread:
- Primary: emit exposure COUNTERS (metrics) at gateway with required dims: org_id/project_id/experiment_id/variant_id/route_id/region/deployment_mode/result/schema_version
- Secondary: sampled debug exposure EVENTS (1%) internal-only, 14-day retention, include request_id hash + idempotency_key_hash for dedupe debugging
- Sticky key handling: HMAC salted hash only, never store raw header, docs/copy warn against PII
- Console queries aggregated rollups only; no raw exposure access

Priya Natarajan: This direction makes sense. Please capture as ADR with explicit non-goals and data access model. Also align with Security on the debug dataset retention.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: If you do metrics counters, make sure tag set is identical across gateway/runtime so we can join latency + cost by experiment/variant.

Logan Wright: I’ll add a cardinality review checklist and ingestion validation rules. @Jada Williams ping me when ADR is ready and I’ll sign off.

Kevin Osei: I’ll confirm retention numbers with compliance and update the audit-log export guidance (SIEM). Exposure metrics won’t go to SIEM; audit events will.

Jada Williams: Thanks all. Action items:
- Jada: update ADR draft w/ metrics-first exposure + sampled debug events + retention/access controls
- Jordan: spec sticky hash (HMAC) + allowed input fields
- Logan/Allison: tag allowlist + cardinality caps + “route_id” requirement
- Marcus/Naomi: privacy language + docs/copy constraints
Will post updated doc here for final review.
